summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would set minimum marine engineering and electro-technical certification standards and require marine regulations to conform to those training and examination requirements.
It would extend the specified standards to commercial vessels of at least 500 gross registered tonnes or propulsion power of at least 3000 kW.
The substantive rules would begin on proclamation or after 18 months if not proclaimed, with alternative training pathways and recognition requirements for overseas qualifications.
changes: Engineering certification instruments would be confined to engineering certification and incidental matters.
Engineers in Classes 1, 2 and 3 would need to pass an oral examination.
Foreign qualification holders would face Australian examination requirements before receiving a competency certificate.
The Principal Examiner would personally audit training colleges and bodies, without delegating that power.
summary.affected: Marine engineers, electro-technical personnel, examiners, marine training providers and operators of covered commercial vessels are affected.
